response_json.request: Add chamfer to main/biggest cylindrical section of Heatbreak body/component. The chamfer should be same size as present on top of the part, but should be added to the lower edge of the cylinder. This should allow easier insertion of the part during assembly.

parameters.chamfer_size: Same size as the existing chamfer present on the top of the part.

actions.target: The lower edge of the main/biggest cylindrical section of the Heatbreak body/component.
actions.relational_constraint: Apply the chamfer to the lower edge of the same cylinder and match its size to the chamfer already present on the top of the part.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the Heatbreak body/component, its main or largest cylindrical section, the lower edge of that cylinder, and the existing top chamfer whose size must be matched.
steps: Isolate section S03, the Stepped cylindrical interface pin, which corresponds to the silver central Heatbreak component visible in the multiview images. Confirm it by its long smooth cylindrical body, axial passage, annular shoulders, and reduced or threaded lower end.

Identify face 0041, Main sleeve cylinder, Brep_id FACE 749. This is the principal and largest external locating cylinder of the Heatbreak and is the cylindrical surface that most directly controls insertion into its mating bore.

Identify face 0040, Sleeve shoulder, Brep_id FACE 769. Select the complete circular lower boundary edge shared by face 0041 and face 0040; this is the lower leading edge of the main sleeve cylinder and is the edge to be modified.

Use face 0042, Upper shoulder, Brep_id FACE 771, and the adjacent existing upper-edge chamfer geometry as the reference end of the same principal cylindrical section. Inspect the detailed B-rep or native feature history to identify the small conical chamfer face adjacent to that upper circular edge.

Measure or retrieve the existing upper chamfer definition. Match its chamfer type and size exactly, including equal-distance dimensions for a symmetric chamfer or the distance-and-angle values if the existing feature is defined asymmetrically.

If a parametric feature history is available, create a new Chamfer feature after the main sleeve and shoulder geometry. Select only the circular edge at the intersection of FACE 749 and FACE 769 and link the new chamfer dimension to the parameter controlling the existing upper chamfer.

If direct B-rep editing is required, apply an edge chamfer to the same circular lower edge using the measured upper-chamfer setback. Maintain a continuous conical transition around the full circumference and preserve the coaxial relationship between the chamfer, main sleeve cylinder, shoulders, and axial passage.

Orient the chamfer so that material is removed from the lower outside corner, producing a reduced-diameter lead-in toward the lower end. Do not chamfer the axial passage, lower threaded region, or unrelated shoulder edges.

Regenerate the solid and verify that the chamfer terminates within faces 0041 and 0040 without consuming the sleeve shoulder, intersecting the axial passage, or altering the locating diameter over the functional length of the main sleeve.

Check the modified S03 component against its coaxial and contained-in relationship with S02, particularly the central locating interface represented by face 0037, and against its locating relationship with S04. Confirm that the new lower lead-in improves initial alignment while leaving the cylindrical engagement and axial seating shoulders unchanged.

Inspect the result in front, left, right, and top-right isometric views. Confirm that the lower edge of the smooth Heatbreak cylinder now has a uniform chamfer visually and dimensionally equal to the existing chamfer at the upper end of that cylindrical section.

intention: Allow easier insertion of the part during assembly.
